title: A Bridge for the Regiment
premise: In 1899, the port town of Saltmere is requisitioned by the colonial army, and Corporal-Adjutant Hale demands the trading company's ledger — a book that records not just debts but the true names, origins, and illegal indentures of every diver in the fleet. Coral Voss, who has spent ten years as the company's invisible record-keeper, realizes the ledger will be used to conscript or deport the people he grew up with, including Sefa, the diver he secretly loves and whose freedom was bought with a forged entry only Coral can prove. Over one winter, Coral copies, alters, and finally steals the evidence, smuggling it past three checkpoints with help from a disgraced sergeant and the company's own corrupt director, each of whom wants the truth for different reasons. At the century's turning, Coral delivers the ledger to the naval magistrate at the cost of his own protected position, exposing the company and choosing love and truth over the safety of silence.
about_author: Petra Okafor is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing colonial shipping records before turning to fiction full-time. She writes historical novels about the people history filed under 'miscellaneous,' and lives near a tidal estuary she refuses to swim in.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Coral Voss, POV. Ten years after his father's drowning, Coral keeps the company's ledgers in Saltmere, invisible and indispensable. He watches Sefa dive for pearls and says nothing about the debt entries that keep her bound. Emotional beat: the quiet ache of a man fluent in silence.

chapters.title: Gunboats at Dawn
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. The colonial army requisitions Saltmere; soldiers occupy the counting house and Director Brannock surrenders the master ledger without a fight. Coral realizes every diver's true name and forged indenture is now in military hands. Beat: dread arriving faster than understanding.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Knows
chapters.summary: Coral, POV, with a brief Sefa interlude. Coral memorizes the ledger's structure by lamplight, discovering that Sefa's manumission paper rests on an entry he himself altered years ago to protect her. Beat: guilt that his kindness left a trail.

chapters.title: Corporal-Adjutant Hale
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The adjutant interviews Coral, probing for discrepancies between ledger and census. Hale is not cruel but ambitious; he needs one clean prosecution to earn a transfer. Beat: the reader sees Coral through predator's eyes.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Coral maps the route any evidence must travel: the harbor gate, the customs house, and the fort bridge — the last crossing into magistrate territory. He tells no one. Beat: cold clarity replacing fear.

chapters.title: Sefa's Question
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. Sefa confronts Coral about why soldiers copy names from the company books, forcing him to lie badly for the first time in ten years. She notices. Beat: the first crack between them, and the first honesty underneath it.

chapters.title: Brannock's Bargain
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Director Brannock privately offers Coral escape papers if he helps destroy incriminating pages — protecting the company, damning the divers. Coral pretends to consider. Beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Sergeant Who Drowned
chapters.summary: Sergeant Ives, POV. Disgraced and half-drunk, Ives reveals he once falsified a drowning report for Brannock — Coral's father's report. He offers Coral the original in exchange for passage off the rock. Beat: grief weaponized, then shared.

chapters.title: Copying by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Over four nights Coral hand-copies the ledger, altering nothing yet, learning which pages Hale has already flagged. Sefa nearly catches him; he confesses everything except his feelings. Beat: intimacy built on shared risk.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Harbor Gate
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Coral sews copied pages into a diving-weight bag Sefa carries through the gate; a soldier's casual search nearly finds them. Beat: terror compressed into ninety seconds, then exhale.

chapters.title: Hale Closes In
chapters.summary: Hale, POV. Hale discovers a page count discrepancy and begins interviewing clerks. He suspects the 'quiet one' but lacks proof. Beat: the hunter's patience, more frightening than rage.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. A diver is conscripted using his ledger entry; the fleet refuses to put out. Sefa organizes a work slowdown, and Coral must decide whether to warn her that resistance gives Hale his pretext. Beat: loyalty pulling against strategy.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Ives, POV. Ives volunteers for customs duty and waves Coral's cargo through, then burns his own falsified report as payment of conscience. Beat: a corrupt man buying back his soul in small coin.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Counting House
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Brannock, cornered by Hale, trades Coral's name for his own immunity. Coral learns he has days, not weeks. Beat: the floor dropping out; invisibility failing completely.

chapters.title: What Silence Costs
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. Sefa learns Coral knew her indenture was forged all along and never told her. Her fury is not about the secret but the pity beneath it. Beat: love interrogated honestly for the first time.

chapters.title: The Original
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Coral steals the master ledger itself from under Hale's desk during the garrison's New Year preparations, replacing it with his own fair copy — the forgery of his life. Beat: the invisible man becoming maximally visible.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Fort Bridge
chapters.summary: Coral and Ives, alternating POV. The bridge crossing at night; a sentry challenges them, Ives draws attention to himself and is arrested so Coral can pass. Beat: sacrifice as the toll of truth.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Door
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Coral reaches the naval magistrate as the old year dies, presenting the ledger and testimony. The magistrate hesitates — the company has friends. Beat: hope balanced on procedure.

chapters.title: Century's Turning
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. As midnight fireworks mark 1900, marines arrive in Saltmere with writs; Hale, ordered to stand down, chooses duty over ambition and surrenders the garrison's records. Beat: power bending, imperfectly, to law.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Brannock is taken; the indentures are voided one by one as names are read aloud on the quay. Coral stands among the counted instead of the counters. Beat: vindication without triumph.

chapters.title: Free Water
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. Sefa dives unbound for the first time, and afterward finds Coral waiting — not asking forgiveness, offering partnership. She accepts neither quickly nor cheaply. Beat: love rebuilt on equal ground.

chapters.title: A Bridge for the Regiment
chapters.summary: Coral, POV, epilogue. Years later, Coral runs a school for scribes teaching that every record can be questioned; the fort bridge bears a plaque naming Ives. Coral finally writes his own true name in a book. Beat: silence ended, voice found.
